research: continuous Gaussian phase hyperparameter importance posterior plus conditional latent phases and calibrated HOM nuisance
type: synthetic conventional quantum-optics and statistics; no photon identity experiments

sampling.hyper_prior: uniform in (log walk_sd,log read_sd,bias) in a bounded region
sampling.proposal: Laplace-Hessian Gaussian scaled 1.4, with exact sensor-likelihood importance weights
sampling.phase: conditional Gaussian phase path with analytic precision matrix
sampling.optical: calibrated physical source, detector, PNR and electronics samples; near/far optical binomial likelihood
sampling.interval: Bayesian equal-tail 95% credible interval, empirical fixed-truth coverage

conclusions: Continuous hyperparameter uncertainty increased the widths of the Bayesian credible intervals and empirical coverage for three tested synthetic settings.
None of the coverages proves universal 95% frequentist coverage, especially with 70 or 50 outer simulations.
Non-Gaussian outlier example is not sufficient to prove robustness against arbitrary readout misspecification.
No independent experimentally testable prediction of persistent historical photon individuality.
